title: 非线性电阻的分类：静态电阻与动态电阻
statement: 非线性电阻 N 的特性为 i = v + 0.5v³（v 单位 V，i 单位 A，关联参考方向），它直接接在 V_s = 2 V 的直流电压源上。
判断这个电阻属于哪一类，并求工作点电流 I_Q、工作点处的静态电阻 R = V_Q/I_Q、动态电阻 R_d = dv/di 以及 N 吸收的功率。

questions.ask: N 是哪一类非线性电阻？
choices: 既是电压控制型又是电流控制型（单调型）
既不是压控型也不是流控型
choiceExplain: i 确实是 v 的单值函数，但还不止于此：di/dv = 1 + 1.5v² > 0，曲线单调。
v 也确实是 i 的单值函数；但还要检查反过来 i 是不是 v 的单值函数。
对。i 随 v 严格单调增加（di/dv = 1 + 1.5v² > 0），所以给定 v 有唯一的 i，给定 i 也有唯一的 v：单调型电阻既是压控型又是流控型。
非线性不等于没有单值函数关系：题中的 i = v + 0.5v³ 本身就是一个单值函数。
questions.explain: 压控型：i 是 v 的单值函数 i = f(v)；流控型：v 是 i 的单值函数 v = h(i)。严格单调的特性两者都满足。

questions.ask: N 是双向（对称）电阻吗？即把它的两个端子对调接入电路，电路的工作情况是否不变？
choices: 是：f(−v) = −f(v)，特性曲线关于原点对称
不是：只有线性电阻才是双向的
choiceExplain: 对。−v + 0.5(−v)³ = −(v + 0.5v³)，曲线关于原点对称，两个端子可以互换。二极管就不是双向的。
非线性电阻也可以是双向的，判据是曲线是否关于原点对称。
questions.explain: 双向电阻：i = f(v) 满足 f(−v) = −f(v)。这里是奇函数，所以是双向的。
电压源直接加在 N 上，V_Q = 2 V：I_Q = 2 + 0.5 × 2³ = 6 A。
R = 2/6 ≈ 0.3333 Ω：工作点与原点连线的斜率的倒数。

questions.ask: 动态电阻 R_d = dv/di（在 Q 点）= ?
questions.explain: di/dv = 1 + 1.5v² = 7 S（v = 2 V），R_d = 1/7 ≈ 0.1429 Ω：Q 点切线斜率的倒数，比静态电阻小。
P = V_Q·I_Q = 2 × 6 = 12 W。功率总是用工作点的 V_Q、I_Q 计算，不能用 R_d。

hints: 分类看函数关系：给定 v 是否只有一个 i？给定 i 是否只有一个 v？看一看 di/dv 的符号。
静态电阻是 Q 点与原点连线的“斜率”V/I，动态电阻是 Q 点切线的斜率 dv/di。
di/dv = 1 + 1.5v²，在 v = 2 V 处求值。
solution: **分类。** di/dv = 1 + 1.5v² > 0，特性严格单调：既是压控型（i = f(v)），又是流控型（v = h(i)）。f(−v) = −f(v)，曲线关于原点对称，是**双向**电阻。
**动态电阻。** di/dv|_{Q} = 1 + 1.5 × 4 = 7 S，R_d = **1/7 ≈ 0.1429 Ω**。两者都随工作点变化；线性电阻的 R = R_d 处处相同。
**检查：** 从图上看，Q 点（2 V，6 A）处切线比原点连线更陡，所以 R_d < R ✓。

en.title: Classifying a nonlinear resistor: static and dynamic resistance
statement: The nonlinear resistor N has the characteristic i = v + 0.5v³ (v in V, i in A, passive convention) and is connected directly to a DC voltage source V_s = 2 V.
Classify the resistor and find the operating current I_Q, the static resistance R = V_Q/I_Q at the operating point, the dynamic resistance R_d = dv/di and the power absorbed by N.

questions.ask: Which kind of nonlinear resistor is N?
choiceExplain: i is indeed a single-valued function of v, but there is more: di/dv = 1 + 1.5v² > 0, the curve is monotonic.
v is indeed a single-valued function of i; but you also need to check whether i is a single-valued function of v.
Right. i increases strictly with v (di/dv = 1 + 1.5v² > 0), so each v gives one i and each i gives one v: a monotonic resistor is both voltage- and current-controlled.
Non-linear does not mean there is no single-valued relation: the given i = v + 0.5v³ is itself one.
questions.explain: Voltage-controlled: i is a single-valued function i = f(v); current-controlled: v is a single-valued function v = h(i). A strictly monotonic characteristic is both.

questions.ask: Is N bilateral, i.e. does the circuit behave the same if its two terminals are swapped?
choices: yes: f(−v) = −f(v), the curve is symmetric about the origin
no: only linear resistors are bilateral
choiceExplain: Right. −v + 0.5(−v)³ = −(v + 0.5v³): the curve is symmetric about the origin, so the terminals can be swapped. A diode is not bilateral.
A nonlinear resistor can be bilateral too; the test is symmetry of the curve about the origin.
questions.explain: Bilateral: i = f(v) with f(−v) = −f(v). Here f is odd, so N is bilateral.
The source is directly across N, so V_Q = 2 V: I_Q = 2 + 0.5 × 2³ = 6 A.
R = 2/6 ≈ 0.3333 Ω: the reciprocal slope of the line from the origin to Q.
di/dv = 1 + 1.5v² = 7 S at v = 2 V, so R_d = 1/7 ≈ 0.1429 Ω: the reciprocal slope of the tangent at Q, smaller than the static resistance.
P = V_Q·I_Q = 2 × 6 = 12 W. Power always uses the operating values V_Q, I_Q, never R_d.

hints: Classify by the functional relation: does a given v give one i only? Does a given i give one v only? Look at the sign of di/dv.
The static resistance is the "slope" V/I of the line from the origin to Q; the dynamic resistance is the slope dv/di of the tangent at Q.
di/dv = 1 + 1.5v²; evaluate it at v = 2 V.
solution: **Classification.** di/dv = 1 + 1.5v² > 0, so the characteristic is strictly monotonic: N is voltage-controlled (i = f(v)) and current-controlled (v = h(i)). f(−v) = −f(v), the curve is symmetric about the origin: N is **bilateral**.
**Operating point.** V_Q = V_s = 2 V, I_Q = 2 + 0.5 × 8 = **6 A**.
**Dynamic resistance.** di/dv at Q = 1 + 1.5 × 4 = 7 S, R_d = **1/7 ≈ 0.1429 Ω**. Both depend on the operating point; for a linear resistor R = R_d everywhere.
**Check:** on the plot the tangent at Q (2 V, 6 A) is steeper than the line from the origin, so R_d < R ✓.
